problem.text: Explicit single-device loading performed immediate module loads, unlike autosplit loading, which already bracketed eligible modules with deferred loading.

reasoning.text: The change reuses the existing module-scoped batching lifecycle rather than introducing another loader. Reduced per-tensor loading overhead is a plausible rationale, not a measured improvement.

impact.text: For eligible modules, _load_single now begins deferral, constructs the module, and flushes pending reads before advancing progress. CPU-preferred placement remains unchanged.

source_notes.text: The earlier deferred-loader entry explicitly identified single-device loading as not adopting this lifecycle.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns extension import failure; issue #33, “Error converting model,” ultimately reports too many open files during conversion. Their relevance here is inferred only from model.py and Safetensors-loader overlap, respectively; neither establishes motivation or validation for this change.

limitations: No repository loading implementation or CUDA kernel was executed; throughput, peak memory and stream behavior remain unmeasured.
The scalar check models chunk and pair coverage only, not conversion rounding or zero-block CUDA launch behavior.
Compatibility across every module constructor and checkpoint was not established.

chapters.title: Deferred loading for explicit single-device placement

claims.text: load_gen selects _load_single when device is explicitly supplied; load consumes that generator. This is distinct from autosplit, even when autosplit happens to use only one GPU.

Eligibility is recursive: leaves permit deferral and composites require all children to permit it. Sliced Linear instances and multi-slice GatedMLP instances opt out. Packed EXL3 su/sv reads and fused FP16 weight reads explicitly bypass deferral where values are needed during construction.

Only mt_fread switches to deferred reads; the Python backend and no_defer requests stay immediate. Deferred get_tensor returns allocated destinations and records pending transfers. Transposition, padding and FP32-to-FP16 conversion may require temporary storage alongside the final allocation.

The flush groups requests by CPU/CUDA and filename, sorts tensors by descending byte size, and splits transfers into at most 2 MiB jobs. CUDA workers stage file bytes through pinned host buffers. Temporary tensors are subsequently transposed as needed and copied into destination regions; successful completion clears deferred state.

The inherited odd-element BF16 CUDA conversion gap remains unchanged and becomes reachable through eligible explicit-device loads. A scalar transcription covered all two elements for an even tensor, but left one uncovered for both three elements and 1,048,577 elements spanning two chunks.

findings.description: The unchanged deferred CUDA BF16 converter processes pairs only; adopting it for explicit-device loading extends exposure to its missing odd-element tail.
findings.trigger: An eligible module requests a file-backed, odd-element BF16 tensor on CUDA through mt_fread with conversion to FP16 enabled and without no_defer.
findings.expected_behavior: Every element is converted to FP16 before consumption.
findings.actual_behavior: The helper launches conversion for numel / 2 pairs, leaving the final odd element unconverted. A one-element final chunk computes zero launch blocks; runtime handling is untested.

verification.description: Whole-parent-tree search locates the direct call in stloader_deferred_cuda. Inspection traces it through end_deferred_load and the newly bracketed _load_single. The task changes only model.py, carrying over the converter unchanged.
verification.limits: Conditional reach only; no affected checkpoint was demonstrated.

verification.description: Standard-library Python modeled the inspected 2 MiB chunking and integer pair counts for even, odd and multi-chunk tensors.
verification.limits: Not execution of the repository kernel; bounded integer arithmetic does not test GPU conversion or synchronization.

annotation.summary: Extends module-scoped deferred loading to explicit single-device loads, preserving eligibility and placement rules; performance is unmeasured and the inherited odd-element BF16 conversion gap persists.

 covered=sum(2*((b//2)//2) for b in sizes)
